name: Kilimanjaro — Rainforest
tagline: Machame Gate to Shira. The first two zones of the mountain.

cairns.title: Machame Gate
cairns.body: Every Machame climb starts here, in cultivated foothills of coffee and banana below the park boundary. Beyond the gate the road ends. From this point the mountain is climbed on foot, and everything that goes up — food, tents, water — is carried by the guides and porters who make the route possible.

cairns.title: The Cloud Forest
cairns.body: Kilimanjaro makes its own weather. Warm air rising off the plains condenses against the slope and falls here, feeding a montane rainforest that soaks the first day of the climb. This band of forest is the mountain's water tower: streams born under this canopy supply the towns for miles around.

cairns.title: Black-and-White Colobus
cairns.body: A long-tailed monkey with a white mantle draped over black fur, usually spotted as movement high in the canopy rather than as an animal. Colobus live almost entirely on leaves, and have a chambered stomach to ferment them — one of the few primates that can make a living on food most animals can't digest.

cairns.title: Hartlaub's Turaco
cairns.body: You'll hear a hoarse barking call in the canopy long before you see anything. When it flies, the wings flash deep crimson — a pigment called turacin, which is unusual because most red in birds comes from diet, and this one is made by the bird itself.

cairns.title: Machame Camp
cairns.body: The first camp, set right at the top edge of the forest. Walk a few minutes past it and the canopy stops as if cut with a line — from here on the mountain is open, the air is thinner and colder, and on a clear night the lights of Moshi are visible far below.

cairns.title: Heath & Moorland
cairns.body: Above the forest the mountain turns to open heath: tussock grass, heather grown to the size of small trees, and everlasting flowers that stay dry and papery on the stem. Days are hot in direct sun and nights fall below freezing — the daily swing here is wider than the seasons.

cairns.title: Giant Groundsel
cairns.body: A plant found on this mountain and almost nowhere else — a thick trunk topped with a rosette of cabbage-like leaves, standing several metres tall. It insulates itself by keeping its dead leaves wrapped around the trunk, and folds the living rosette closed at night to protect the growing bud from frost.

cairns.title: Shira Plateau
cairns.body: A broad, flat plain that is the collapsed remains of Shira — the oldest of Kilimanjaro's three volcanic cones, extinct and eroded long before the summit cone existed. You are walking across the floor of a mountain that is no longer there, with Kibo ahead.
